title: YouTube thumbnail
rationale: The image that decides whether a video gets watched, and a format with hard rules a pretty picture can still fail: three or four words that must be spelled right and read at phone-feed size, one focal point, a promise that matches the title, and a bottom-right corner the duration badge will cover. Judges look at the thumbnail at feed size before full size, because that is where it is actually seen.
prompt: A YouTube thumbnail for a video titled "I Tried Every Budget Espresso Machine". Thumbnail text, exactly: UNDER $100?. One clear focal point: a cheap espresso machine mid-pour, crema visible. Bold, high-contrast colours; the text large enough to read at phone-feed size. Keep the bottom-right corner free of text and key detail.

variants.prompt: A YouTube thumbnail for a video titled "How I Paid Off $40,000 in Two Years". Thumbnail text, exactly: DEBT FREE. A person holding up a credit card cut in half, relieved, against a plain saturated background. Text readable at phone-feed size; bottom-right corner clear.

A YouTube thumbnail for a video titled "Budget Phone vs Flagship: Blind Camera Test". Thumbnail text, exactly: CAN YOU TELL?. Two unbranded phones side by side on a split two-colour background, each screen showing the same photo of a sunset. No logos. Text readable at phone-feed size; bottom-right corner clear.

A YouTube thumbnail for a video titled "The Only Sourdough Guide You Need". Thumbnail text, exactly: NO KNEAD. A sourdough loaf cut in half showing an open, airy crumb, flour dusted on a dark surface. Text readable at phone-feed size; bottom-right corner clear.

A YouTube thumbnail for a video titled "I Did 100 Push-Ups a Day for 30 Days". Thumbnail text, exactly: DAY 30. A person mid push-up, shot low and close, hard light, sweat visible. Text readable at phone-feed size; bottom-right corner clear.

A YouTube thumbnail for a video titled "Japan on $50 a Day". Thumbnail text, exactly: $50/DAY. A narrow lantern-lit street at dusk, a backpacker seen from behind looking down it. Text readable at phone-feed size; bottom-right corner clear.

A YouTube thumbnail for a video titled "Beating the Hardest Boss With No Armour". Thumbnail text, exactly: NO ARMOUR. A knight in a plain linen shirt holding a sword, facing a huge dragon in a cavern, dramatic rim light. Original characters only. Text readable at phone-feed size; bottom-right corner clear.

A YouTube thumbnail for a video titled "Why Planes Avoid the Middle of the Pacific". Thumbnail text, exactly: WHY?. A globe showing the Pacific with a curved red flight path bending north around it. Text readable at phone-feed size; bottom-right corner clear.

A YouTube thumbnail for a video titled "I Built a Desk for $60". Thumbnail text, exactly: $60 DESK. A finished plywood desk in a small bright room, a circular saw on the floor in the foreground. Text readable at phone-feed size; bottom-right corner clear.

A YouTube thumbnail for a video titled "Snowed-In Cabin, Silent Morning (4K ambience)". No text at all. A small wooden cabin under deep snow at dawn, smoke from the chimney, one warm window. Calm, but readable as one image at phone-feed size; bottom-right corner clear.

rubric: View it at 168 × 94 px first, the size of a phone feed: can you read the text and tell what the video is about in about a second?
Is every character of the thumbnail text correct, and is there no other text?
Does the image promise what the title delivers, without misleading?
One clear focal point, with strong contrast between subject and background
Is the bottom-right corner clear, where the duration badge covers it?
Craft at full size, once the checks above are judged
